title: Beyond the Next-Generation Matrix Criterion: Global Stability, Multistability and Spatial Diffusion in Production and Threshold Networks
content: This paper uses Jacobian triangularity on siphon faces and the Metzler property of the transverse block to study positive production networks, including higher-order SIS, simplicial contagion, threshold and firing-rate models. The main results are: (1) First-order production terms in the absent variables determine the transverse invasion matrices. Terms at least quadratic in those variables leave these matrices unchanged at a fixed resident state, but can create bistability. (2) For threshold networks with a prescribed response-slope bound, a sharp spectral threshold separates global convergence for every response from the possibility of arbitrarily many stable equilibria. (3) Adding diagonal diffusion to threshold networks preserves the spectral threshold in (2) and yields an upper bound on spreading speeds. At a spatially constant boundary equilibrium, the transverse invasion matrix determines a positive linear spreading speed when the invasion number exceeds one, the matrix is irreducible and at least one absent species diffuses. (4) Invariant group partitions give exact reduced equations and preserve local exponential equilibrium stability in cooperative networks. Saddle-node and cusp bifurcations also lift to the full network when the full Jacobian has a simple zero eigenvalue and all remaining eigenvalues have negative real parts. (5) Responses of the form $\Phi(q)=\varphi(q)/(1+\varphi(q))$, where $\varphi$ is a nonzero polynomial with nonnegative coefficients and $\varphi(0)=0$, preserve the siphon lattice as those coefficients vary. For $\dot x=-x+\Phi(x)$, degree four is the minimum allowing a hyperbolically stable origin and a positive nondegenerate cusp. (6) Added production monomials preserve specified siphons when each monomial contains a variable from every such siphon containing the species being produced. A three-population example has two overlapping minimal siphons, nonzero boundary equilibria with distinct invasion numbers, and at least eight stable equilibria coexisting with an interior cusp; at least nine stable equilibria occur nearby. (7) Weighted sums of absent populations give extinction certificates, while state-dependent weighted norms characterize uniform exponential stability of cooperative variational equations. Lyapunov–Volterra functions (Fenchel–Bregman divergences) give explicit subsets of basins of attraction, with or without diffusion.
